item.title: [EU Observer] Tinned food and three days of bottled water? Fine. But European citizens stockpiling ignores a grim factor: your neighbours will become your enemies
item.description: A friend of mine recently proudly showed me her cellar, stocked with three to four weeks of water and food. “Of course, we’ll be sharing it with the neighbours” she said.But the only thought in my head was “After three to four weeks of no food, no electricity, no internet and no water, you’ll be fighting your neighbours off, no inviting them in.”

item.title: [EU Observer] How the rescue of 28 people from a makeshift dinghy in a stormy Mediterranean unfolded – exposing the lethal reality of EU border policy
item.description: A small, homemade, dinghy hoped to escape the deadly EU-sponsored Libyan coastguard by making its way north during one of the stormiest seasons in the Mediterranean Sea. Their successful rescue by volunteers contrasts with the reception they received from Italian authorities, prior to even touching European land.

item.title: [DW] Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s centre parties are collapsing – and, for the first time, the far-right are collaborating, rather than fighting
item.description: Opinion polling from the Pew Research Center found that 69 percent of the French population is dissatisfied with democracy, Italy 62 percent, Poland 47 percent and Spain 68 percent. All are facing upcoming elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] Finnish president Stubb joins list of EU leaders seeking to tame Putin, in a 90-minute Kremlin phone call that caused a rift with Denmark
item.description: The Finnish-Norwegian call was "not coordinated with any of us [allies]" in advance, said Denmark's Mette Frederiksen on Tuesday - directly contradicting Finland's Alexander Stubb and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre. "I really don't understand what these two countries think can be achieved this way," she said.

item.title: [EU Observer] Two graphs and one map show that Russia is not currently winning the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,706)
item.description: Analysts tracking satellite images, daily engagements and shifting frontlines say the war has frozen into a deadly stalemate.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
